claims.evidence: Witness report shows a partially disassembled car engine bay/engine assembly with no readable brand/model label; make/model/variant not readable.

risks.risk: Engine may be incomplete (missing key components like ECU, alternator, starter, sensors, wiring harness, turbo/supercharger if applicable), which can make it unusable or require extra spend.
risks.proof: A clear photo/video showing the full engine assembly laid out with a checklist view of ECU, alternator, starter, sensors, wiring harness, and all major accessories present (and any missing parts clearly shown).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a used, partially disassembled/incomplete engine with unknown functionality.

risks.risk: Unknown running condition (may not start, may have internal damage, low compression, or timing/valvetrain issues).
risks.proof: A short video of the engine being started (or at minimum a compression test sheet/results and a running video showing idle stability).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven/unknown working condition (worst-case: non-running).

risks.risk: Possible major leaks or heavy wear indicated by oil/grease staining and dirt; could be oil/coolant leaks or seepage from seals/gaskets.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of suspected leak points (oil pan area, valve cover, timing cover, coolant hoses/radiator connections) plus a wipe-and-recheck clip showing fresh leaks after running.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as having potential leaks/maintenance needs.

risks.risk: Parts may be separated or removed from the main block (risk of wrong parts, mismatched components, or damage during removal).
risks.proof: A photo sequence showing each removed component labeled and matched to the engine (and confirmation that all parts belong to the same engine/variant).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as partially disassembled with risk of mismatched/wrong parts.

risks.risk: Cooling system and hoses/radiator-related components may be missing or degraded, affecting reliability after installation.
risks.proof: Photos showing all cooling-related components included (radiator, hoses, thermostat housing, water pump if present) and their condition (no cracks/bulges).

risks.risk: Compatibility risk: even if it’s claimed as a specific Lexus LX460 Japan engine, the exact variant/fitment may differ (year/engine code), causing mounting/electrical mismatch.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine code/ID plate and matching VIN/engine code confirmation (or a document showing engine code and year/variant).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as generic/unknown fitment requiring verification.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photos of any engine ID/label/engine code plate (readable) and where it is located on the engine.
Video of the engine being started (or compression test results with readings).
Photos showing the full list of included parts: ECU, alternator, starter, sensors, wiring harness, and any turbo/supercharger (if applicable).
A missing-parts list from the seller (what is not included) with photos of what remains.
Close-up photos of suspected leak points and a wipe-and-recheck clip after running (if possible).
Photos of cooling system components included (hoses, thermostat housing, water pump/radiator connections) and their condition.
response.reason: The witness can identify it only as a used, partially disassembled car engine assembly with no readable make/model; the seller’s specific Lexus LX460 Japan claim is not verifiable from the report. So it can be priced at the worst case for an incomplete/unknown-working engine, pending the proof requests.
